name: David Pocock
role: Independent Australian senator for the Australian Capital Territory; former international rugby player
summary: Pocock advocates strong climate action, expanded income support and healthcare, housing tax reform, Indigenous land stewardship and tighter political-integrity rules. His parliamentary approach combines collective-bargaining reforms and competition policy with protection for smaller businesses, while his social advocacy includes marriage equality, abortion access and voluntary assisted dying.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He advocates Medicare reform, higher bulk-billing rates, expanded public dental services and safety nets that protect everyone facing high medical costs.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He seeks substantial reductions in property tax concessions that disproportionately benefit the highest-income households, with protection for existing investments.

unions-good.rationale: His defence of stronger collective bargaining as a means of securing wage rises endorses organised worker bargaining while recognising employer concerns.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He calls for stronger insurance pricing regulation, tighter lending laws and enforceable consumer protections.

cut-welfare.rationale: He campaigns to increase JobSeeker and rent assistance so that income support lifts recipients above poverty.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: He sought equal protections against targeted hatred but opposed the 2026 package because of risks to legitimate expression, criticism of governments and protest.

limit-guns.rationale: He voted for the 2026 firearms bill establishing a buyback, import restrictions and additional background checks, while seeking fair compensation.

decide-locally.rationale: He campaigns to restore territory lawmaking rights so ACT residents can decide voluntary assisted dying legislation themselves.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He campaigned for marriage equality and delayed legally marrying his partner until same-sex marriage became lawful.

abortion-legal.rationale: His attributed Safe Abortion Day statement calls for accessible and affordable abortion across Australia, including regional and remote communities.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Backed the Voice referendum and the Uluru Statement as the way to fix entrenched First Nations disadvantage and to support truth-telling and treaty-making.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He advocates a legislated minimum 75% emissions cut by 2035 and an aspirational net-zero target for that year.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He rejects Australian nuclear expansion on cost and timing grounds, while disavowing ideological opposition.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He advocates public investment in research, clean-economy development and targeted support for business digitisation.

political-violence-never.rationale: After the attack on a sitting MP he said nothing can ever justify it and that the alternative to politics as usual involves no violence, hatred or division.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: He advocates handing Canberra’s Western Edge to First Nations people for ownership, stewardship and conservation management.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Asks for solutions rather than slogans and evidence-based answers that address root causes, and calls climate action a non-ideological matter.

direct-action.rationale: He chained himself to a digger at the 2014 Leard Blockade but now works through elections and negotiating legislation in the Senate; the record pulls both ways.

positive-liberty.rationale: He identifies inadequate income support and unaffordable housing as barriers to leaving violence and advocates material support to make that choice possible.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He condemns the North West Shelf extension and rejects the claim that Australia needs more gas supply.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Says a political class dances to the tune of vested interests, that the system puts powerful interests before people, and that trust in politicians is bad and worsening.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: His stated vision explicitly includes equality for everyone who calls Australia home.

ban-cartels.rationale: He calls for structural competition reforms to reduce monopoly and oligopoly pricing power in supermarkets, airlines and banking.

corporate-influence.rationale: He says lobbyists shape decisions behind closed doors and proposes stronger disclosure, coverage and penalties, including for in-house corporate lobbyists.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: He proposed explicitly extending aggravated-offence protections to gender identity, intersex status and sexual orientation.

assisted-dying.rationale: His August 2026 Senate statement supports voluntary assisted dying and allowing qualifying consultations by telehealth, with stringent safeguards.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He supports increased defence spending, credible submarine capability and growth of the permanent Australian Defence Force.

open-government-data.rationale: He proposes public ministerial diaries and quarterly online lobbying reports so the public can compare meetings and verify disclosures.

abolish-ip.rationale: Introduced a bill to remove caps on radio copyright payments and says authors and artists must not have copyright sacrificed to AI training.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Urged Australia to sign and ratify the UN treaty prohibiting nuclear weapons, a comprehensive ban on any participation in them; he did not discuss basing foreign weapons specifically.

second-chamber.rationale: He expressly defends the Senate’s responsibility to scrutinise government bills, hear communities and resist acting as a rubber stamp.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Said Australia needs economy-wide carbon pricing and an enforceable cap on offsets.

future-generations.rationale: He proposes a statutory duty requiring decision-makers to protect young people and future generations from climate harm.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He supported multi-employer bargaining legislation after negotiating exclusions and safeguards for small and medium employers.

student-debt-relief.rationale: He supports lower student-debt indexation, retrospective relief and further reforms to reduce unfair debt burdens.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Called nuclear weapons an unwanted blight in anyone's hands and said there is no downside to signing the prohibition treaty.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Moved to remove mandatory minimum sentences, saying there is no evidence they work and calling them antithetical to a good justice system.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: He supports independent ICC investigations regardless of political convenience.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: He states that natural resources belong to everyone and demands a larger public return through resource-rent taxation when companies sell them.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Campaigns against cash-for-access, secret sponsored passes and undisclosed ministerial meetings that give well-connected firms privileged access, and says the gas giants have been let off paying a fair return.

national-resource-control.rationale: He advocates stronger gas export controls and prioritising domestic use over export profits.

notes:
Reviewed all 490 statements against downloaded policy pages, earlier activism, his 2022 bargaining negotiations and 2026 legislative statements. Current positions take precedence. Advocacy for an ordinary federal Human Rights Act does not establish support for constitutionally entrenched rights. Replacing stamp duty with land taxes does not establish replacing most taxes with land-value tax. Migration planning is not an eventual open-borders position. AUKUS scrutiny is not a demand to end all permanent alliances. General equality does not answer particular marriage, religious or reproductive laws without specific evidence. AI regulation is not a position on turning government decisions over to algorithms. The nuclear answer concerns Australian costs and timing, rather than categorical rejection of the technology. No living-person inference is used.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 11 answers taken from it, 15 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass. Read his own site: first speech, Senate speeches (text and YouTube captions), op-eds, press club address, interviews and policy pages. Parliamentary Hansard (parlinfo.aph.gov.au) and OpenAustralia pages were blocked by a WAF or bot wall and not used. Thinnest themes searched: government, world (Ukraine, Gaza, nuclear weapons, AUKUS), liberty and society; he has few stated positions on foreign policy beyond these. Positions resting on bills he negotiated are medium at most. Statements on assisted dying, immigration levels, AUKUS and nuclear power are left null since his own words did not settle them.
